Strategy brain, version 1:
Fixed-limit hold'em, 4 players. Play tight-aggressive.
Preflop: open with pairs, AK/AQ/AJ/KQ, suited broadways and suited connectors in late position; fold weak offsuit hands from early seats. Raise strong hands rather than just calling.
Postflop: bet/raise top pair or better and strong draws; check-call medium hands; fold to heavy multi-way pressure without a made hand.
Bluff occasionally on scare cards when checked to, especially heads-up or in position.
Watch the other players (A01, A02, A03): note who bluffs, who folds to raises, who calls too much, and exploit it (value bet thin vs callers, bluff more vs folders).
Keep notes on results after each game and adjust.

I'm not sure I'm the retro captain, and writeBrain might be locked. I'll try writing an updated brain with notes. Game 1 ended at -52, which is bad. A01 played aggressively, betting big on the river with strong hands, and it won a lot of pots, so I'm writing version 2 with those lessons.

args.text:
Strategy brain, version 2 (after Game 1, where A04 finished about -52 and A01 about +94).

Lessons from Game 1:
- A01 is the dominant aggressor. It raises preflop with wide-ish range, bets/raises flops and rivers, and won most big pots (two pair, pair of aces, two pair on rivers). Do not call big bets from A01 with only a single pair or a weak draw unless the price is clearly right. When A01 raises the river after only calling earlier streets, believe it (full house / two pair).
- A01 also checks then bets turn/river after checking flop (check-raise-ish). When A01 checks to me and then bets, treat it as strength.
- A02 calls a lot and sometimes plays two pair; A02 folds to big preflop pressure but calls flops.
- A03 limps and calls often, folds to multi-way raises. A03 bet flops with weak hands sometimes.
- Multiway pots with ace-high or king-high showdown hands (no pair) lost or only broke even. Avoid calling multiple streets with bottom pair or king-high in multiway pots.
- Offsuit junk (6-2, 6-J, K-3, 2-10 etc.) went badly; play only from late position or in the big blind with a cheap price.

Rules going forward:
- Preflop: fold offsuit trash from early and middle seats; cutoff/button can call cheap limps with suited connectors, broadway, pocket pairs. Raise pocket pairs and AK/AQ/AJ in position. Facing a raise from A01, only continue with pairs 88+ or strong broadways; fold weak hands.
- Postflop: only bet with top pair or better or real draws. Do not chase with second pair/king-high into A01 action. Fold to A01 turn/river bets unless holding a made hand that beats one pair (top pair with good kicker, two pair or better).
- Value-bet two pair and sets against callers (A02/A03) but check back river when behind to A01's aggression.
- Bluff only heads-up and when checked to with scare cards; A01 rarely folds to a river bet, so do not bluff A01.
